gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, priced today, two added 14-inch screens cost less from the maker than the one-screen extender ChatGPT picked. FOPO's S1 dual is $159.99 at fopomonitor.com, while the Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS is $219.99 on Amazon and was $229.49 on ChatGPT's card. Only FOPO's page adds that each S1 screen needs its own video connection.
standout_why: I read the two pages ChatGPT cited: itechguides.com '15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026' and rottenwifi.com '15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026'. Itechguides gives no price for the Duex Max DS, Duex Plus DS or Duex Float 2 Pro. Rottenwifi quotes old sale prices ('~$229.49' for the Max DS and '~$195.49' for the Plus DS) and calls them 'dated price signals'. Neither page names FOPO or Arzopa's E1, and neither says which dual extenders need one video port per screen. deskfinds.com returned 403. ChatGPT's own cards showed retailer prices: $229.49 for the Max DS, $87.99 for the Arzopa A1, and $249.99 and $139.99 for UPERFECT's dual 14-inch, which I couldn't find on uperfect.com.
decides: The finding confirms a split pick instead of ChatGPT's single top pick. For a shopper who wants two added screens and whose laptop has two video-capable ports (USB-C with DisplayPort Alt Mode, or USB-C plus HDMI), our FOPO S1 gives two 14-inch 1080p screens for {after:fopo-s1-dual-14-inch-laptop-screen-extender}, well under $300 and below ChatGPT's dual picks. Each S1 screen needs its own video connection (FOPO's page). So a laptop that drives only one external display lights only one S1 screen without a driver. For that shopper, our Duex Max DS ({after:mobile-pixels-duex-max-ds}) wins: one 14.1-inch screen on one USB-C Alt Mode cable, no driver (our record), and below its $219.99 Amazon price today. On price alone, a freestanding screen wins: the Arzopa A1 is $79.99 at arzopa.com, but it doesn't attach to the laptop. Teamgee's attachable 14-inch screens are $199.99 to $299.99 for one added screen, which is more than our options.
